findings.observation: At 66abacd both comment blocks still state the counts the Request names as wrong. The theme block says: Copying the five neighbouring tags is therefore the single most likely mistake in this file, and: The other five below are correct as they are. The nav-collapse block says: both pre-paint scripts are above the deferred five. The head declares two plain pre-paint tags above SEVEN deferred neighbours, which is the table both readers assert (htmx.min.js, board-dnd.js, board-lane-dnd.js, board-live.js, csrf-upload.js, keyboard.js, form-errors.js). A contributor who reads before she edits is told there are five, and the oracle asserts nine pairs, so the standing instruction beside the tags contradicts the head the suite asserts. P10 is correctly dispositioned NotTested: the correction removes the measurable claim rather than replacing it, and pinning the prose would freeze wording a contributor should be free to improve, so this review is the declared observer of that agreement.
findings.remediation: In the S1 craft, de-number both comment blocks: name the pre-paint FAMILY and the deferred NEIGHBOURS instead of a count, keep every tag, attribute and script order unchanged, and keep the reference to the gate layer that now refuses both arms. Then this reviewer re-reads the two blocks against the nine-pair table.

findings.obligation: The gate answers every head-script shape with exactly one verdict, and the gate documentation agrees with the law it enforces (P12, and the S1 scope-in item on the corrected texts).
findings.observation: The PASSED sentence states one arm only: every head script of the document shell that paints stored state onto the document element is render-blocking - none carries defer, async or type=module (pre-paint-script). Observed at 66abacd by running the gate: exit 0 and that sentence printed verbatim. After S1 the layer also refuses every head script that is NOT a pre-paint script and does not defer, so the sentence a contributor reads on acceptance will understate the law and will not tell her that async and type=module on a plain neighbour are refused. The design Impact row for the gate aggregate already anticipates this: its sentence there may need the second arm named.
findings.remediation: Name the second arm in the same sentence, as prose inside the S1 change: say that every other head script must carry defer. No new layer, no second marker; the existing marker pre-paint-script: and its aggregation test stay as they are.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/canzan-theme-system.feature:331 (scenario A chosen dark screen never flashes light, tags needs-browser and real-io) and crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/served_markup.rs
findings.obligation: Contract test T4: both readers yield the identical nine (src, deferring) pairs for the shipped head, each compared with the same independently written table, so a reader that drifts fails on exactly the side that drifted.
findings.observation: The gate half runs in the default suite and was executed here (cargo test -p xtask check_arch::, exit 101 with the_gate_reads_the_shipped_head_as_the_pre_paint_family_above_its_deferred_neighbours passing). The suite half runs only in the browser lane: its step sits in a needs-browser real-io scenario, and this project skips that lane without the Docker flag, so a drift in the new shared served-markup reader - a fourth deferring attribute it does not know, a quoting form it mis-reads, a tag it skips - can stay unobserved in a normal gate run while the gate half still passes. The pairing then degrades to one observed reader, which is the claim T4 exists to turn from an assertion into an observation. The shared reader itself has no observation in the default suite.
findings.remediation: Keep the served-page comparison where it is, and close the reach either way: record the browser-lane run of the declared command (FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=canzan-theme-system cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --release, browser lane enabled) as named S1 completion evidence for T4, or give the shared reader one fixture-level observation in the default suite over a head string carrying each deferring attribute and quoting form, so reader drift fails fast on this side too. Do not merge the two readers.

observations.text: ROUND 2 at HEAD 2d473dc, opened from the published round-1 review (approved at 66abacd). Scope is only the S1-declared oracle and support bytes that differ from 66abacd. git diff --name-status 66abacd..HEAD over the S1 declaration yields four changed files: xtask/src/check_arch.rs, crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_nav_collapse.rs, crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/mod.rs and crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/nav-collapse-toggle.feature. The other three S1 supports are byte-unchanged: src/support/served_markup.rs, src/steps/feature_canzan_theme.rs and tests/features/canzan-theme-system.feature. Working tree carries only the untracked docs/feature/nav-collapse-icon-rail/.nwdes-drafts/ directory, which was left as it is; no candidate or oracle byte was touched by this review.

THE ORACLE ITSELF IS BYTE-UNCHANGED. mod pre_paint_script_tests extracted from xtask/src/check_arch.rs at both revisions by brace matching: 66abacd sha256 ab6a405246a3a0e341d1577a179d3fd9fe6947143bd35820408c4f1d8ec7bcaa, 45998 bytes; 2d473dc sha256 ab6a405246a3a0e341d1577a179d3fd9fe6947143bd35820408c4f1d8ec7bcaa, 45998 bytes. IDENTICAL. All six diff hunks of check_arch.rs between the two commits are at lines 176, 1814, 1827, 1865, 1886 and 2007, every one of them outside that module, so the production step edited no oracle test file and the round-1 approval of the oracle bytes stands unmodified. The approved oracle is therefore not what changed; the OracleChanged refusal is accounted for by the rule functions beneath it and by the S2 oracle work in two shared support files.

AFFECTED CHECK RERUN, NOT REUSED, because the rule functions under the oracle changed. argv: scripts/test-in-lima.sh env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 cargo test -p xtask check_arch:: at 2d473dc, in the Lima VM. exit 0. stdout: test result: ok. 283 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1 filtered out; finished in 4.79s. stderr: empty. The total is the same 283 as round 1 (277 passed plus 6 failed), so no oracle test was added, removed or renamed, and the six cases that were RED at 66abacd are the six now green. The semantic RED evidence for S1 stays the round-1 execution at 66abacd (exit 101, 6 failed, each an assertion on the promised observation); that run is cited, not restamped, and no new RED execution is claimed.

argv: scripts/test-in-lima.sh env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 cargo check -p foundry-acceptance --all-targets at 2d473dc. exit 0, Finished dev profile in 43.51s, no error and no warning. The S1 supports remain constructible after the S2 oracle work: served_markup.rs is byte-unchanged and is still the ONE owner of the served-head reading, called by crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_canzan_theme.rs (lines 172, 1607, 1686) and crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_nav_collapse.rs (lines 50, 615), with no private copy anywhere in the crate. S1's Replace decision for feature_nav_collapse.rs and its CreateNew owner decision are both preserved.

The two S2-driven support changes do not weaken any S1 obligation. support/mod.rs gained exactly one line, pub mod rail_reading, declared beside pub mod served_markup, which is additive and leaves the S1 reader declared. feature_nav_collapse.rs changed in its rail-probe region only: the diff hunks are at lines 32, 55, 90, 928, 1240, 1346, 1375 and 1551, and the S1-bearing step then_mark_is_stamped_by_a_render_blocking_script with its call to the shared head_scripts (lines 595 to 650) lies in no hunk, so it is byte-unchanged from 66abacd and its round-1 judgment is retained unexamined. nav-collapse-toggle.feature changed only in the keyboard-order scenario, whose premise was restated from a hidden rail to the icon rail (no hidden nav item ever takes the keyboard focus becomes no nav item ever takes the keyboard focus while it is invisible), per ADR-NAV-ICON-RAIL-001; that scenario carries none of S1's obligations P8, P9, P12 or T4. These S2 changes were reviewed and accepted in their own right in docs/feature/nav-collapse-icon-rail/runs/review.oracle.S2.json over three rounds, which this review cites rather than re-judging.

The byte-unchanged step in feature_nav_collapse.rs still carries its own local anti-vacuity arm, deferred_neighbours greater than zero, and that is deliberately NOT a new finding: it is not the arm the Request named (that one was feature_canzan_theme.rs's, and it is now restated over the whole non-pre-paint set and names the offenders), the design assigned P9's whole-set arm to the theme step by its Extend decision, and this guard is scoped to the nav tag's own vacuity rather than to P9. No byte of it changed since the round-1 approval, so reopening it in round 2 would reverse a settled judgment with no new evidence.

The oracle's clause assertions were satisfied by genuine prose, not by keyword stuffing, which is what keeps the round-1 approval meaningful now that the tests are green. Read at 2d473dc: refusal_for_a_script_that_names_the_pair (xtask/src/check_arch.rs:1918) states the src and the attributes carried, that the gate decided BY NAME from comment-stripped source and that source cannot show WHEN the names are touched, CASE ONE remove the attributes with the render-blocking reason, CASE TWO split the stored-state read into its own deferred asset or record a deliberate exception, and the closing warning that dropping the attributes instead would be accepted by this very gate with nothing left observing it; it never claims the asset was watched reading or stamping. refusal_for_a_neighbour_that_does_not_defer (line 1944) names the src, its loading mode, the one remedy add defer, and what to do if the asset really is a pre-paint script. Each of the five clause fragments the oracle checks sits inside a sentence that carries its meaning, so a text passing the oracle genuinely tells the contributor what she needs.

P12 totality is observed over the declared input and nowhere wider. The design declares the driven port as the head region of base.html plus the comment-stripped bytes of each asset under crates/foundry-app/static that the head names, and the twenty-four shapes are three storage values by the document element named or not by four loading modes, all with a /static/ src and a readable asset. The crafter's stated limit, recorded in runs/craft.S1.json, is that a head script whose asset the layer cannot read - an inline script, a runtime-added script, or a src outside /static/ - keeps the pre-existing skip instead of a verdict. That case is outside the declared port and outside the enumerated domain, it is pre-existing rather than introduced, and it is now stated in the layer doc comment, so it is recorded here as a stated limit of the totality claim and not as a finding. Identifiers built at run time stay under-approximated and the neighbour refusal says so.

DISPOSITION OF THE ROUND-1 FINDINGS, read off the new bytes. Finding 1 (implementation, base.html head comments) is RESOLVED: both comment blocks are de-numbered at 2d473dc - the theme block now opens A MEMBER OF THE PRE-PAINT FAMILY OF THIS HEAD and says Copying the deferred neighbours below and The deferred neighbours below are correct as they are; the nav block opens ANOTHER MEMBER OF THE PRE-PAINT FAMILY and says the pre-paint family stays above the deferred neighbours; no count survives in either block, so the stale five is gone and no new number can go stale. Finding 2 (implementation, the aggregate PASSED sentence) is RESOLVED: the sentence at xtask/src/check_arch.rs:179 now reads every head script of the document shell whose asset names a browser store and names documentElement is render-blocking - none carries defer, async or type=module - and every other head script of that shell carries defer, so none of them sits on the render-blocking path for nothing (pre-paint-script); the marker and the layer count are unchanged and no new layer was added. Observed with cargo xtask check-arch exit 0 in round 1 and by reading the new bytes here.

Finding 3 (oracle, the reach of contract test T4's suite half) stays OPEN as a completion obligation. served_markup.rs is byte-unchanged, so no default-suite observation of the shared reader was added, and runs/craft.S1.json records cargo build --release -p foundry-app and the two FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS lanes (canzan-theme-system, nav-collapse-toggle) as NOT RUN, host-owned. The gate half of T4 is executed and green here (the_gate_reads_the_shipped_head_as_the_pre_paint_family_above_its_deferred_neighbours, inside the 283 passed), so the paired reading is half observed. Its remediation is unchanged: record the browser-lane run of the declared acceptance command as named S1 completion evidence for T4, or give the shared reader one fixture-level observation in the default suite. This is non-blocking for craft, which is complete, and remains an open completion obligation for the whole-candidate close. Docker was not run in this review, as the root required.
